findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: spurvik_find_unwrapped_calls, spurvik_scan_live_url, spurvik_batch_scan_domains, spurvik_check_image_c2pa_url · Private data: spurvik_find_unwrapped_calls, spurvik_explain_receipt, spurvik_batch_scan_domains, spurvik_check_image_c2pa_url · Public sink: spurvik_vendor_questionnaire_answers · Destructive: spurvik_find_unwrapped_calls, spurvik_check_image_c2pa_url.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: spurvik_find_unwrapped_calls, spurvik_scan_live_url, spurvik_batch_scan_domains, spurvik_check_image_c2pa_url · Private data: spurvik_find_unwrapped_calls, spurvik_explain_receipt, spurvik_batch_scan_domains, spurvik_check_image_c2pa_url · Public sink: spurvik_vendor_questionnaire_answers · Destructive: spurvik_find_unwrapped_calls, spurvik_check_image_c2pa_url

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "spurvik_setup_snippet" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
